errors.text: The proposed Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V composition consists predominantly of BCC-stabilizing refractory elements, yet no thermodynamic or experimental evidence is provided that annealing at 400-600 °C can produce an FCC solid-solution phase.

The claim that configurational entropy will prevent B2, Laves, or other ordered phases is not generally valid; entropy alone does not override composition-dependent enthalpy and low-temperature ordering tendencies.
The cited studies do not demonstrate the proposed cryogenic SPD followed by low-temperature BCC-to-BCC/FCC separation while retaining sub-50 nm grains.
Cryogenic ECAP of a coarse-grained, low-ductility refractory alloy is assumed feasible without addressing cracking, required pressure, strain path, or attainable accumulated strain.

The falsification experiment does not distinguish Hall-Petch or phase-boundary strengthening from simple solid-solution strengthening because the compared samples differ simultaneously in grain size, deformation state, dislocation density, texture, and phase constitution.
